Photograph: Social Media/Reuters Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Ukraine Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Russian soldier in Crimea shoots comrades and civilians Soldier arrested after shooting; Kyiv comes under ballistic missile attack; more Wildberries hit. What we know on day 1,624 Warren Murray and agencies Tue 4 Aug 2026 21.27 EDT Last modified on Tue 4 Aug 2026 21.28 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Russian soldier ⁠in Crimea ⁠ opened fire ​on comrades, killing one and wounding ⁠another, before shooting civilians and killing ⁠three . Three other ‌people were ‌wounded, said Mikhail Razvozhayev, the Russian-installed ‌governor of the Sevastopol region. He said the attacker had been arrested. “A tragedy in Sevastopol … According to initial information, a soldier opened fire on his fellow servicemen, killing one person, before attacking civilians and killing three of them,” Razvozhayev posted. “All circumstances and causes of the ​incident are being established.” Crimea, a peninsula illegally annexed by Russia from Ukraine in 2014, has for weeks been the target of Ukrainian attacks aimed at disrupting Russian military logistics and cutting off the occupiers’ gasoline and electricity supplies. Russian ballistic missiles ⁠hit Kyiv early on Wednesday, killing ⁠one ​person, injuring 12 and severely damaging buildings in several districts. Air raid alerts remained in place for ​more than an hour. The mayor, ‌Vitali Klitschko, said one warehouse building had been destroyed near the ‌city centre and rescue teams had pulled two people from the ruins. “There may still be people under the rubble.” The attack triggered ⁠an ammonia leak, which was being tackled by emergency crews. Ukrainian drones struck warehouses across Russia including several run ⁠by online retailer Wildberries , local officials said. Wildberries said its ​ warehouse near St Petersburg ‌caught fire ‌with no casualties. In the Tver ‌region, about 180km north-west of Moscow, a Wildberries facility was damaged by drones in the rural area of Emmaus. In the Moscow region , ‌a drone attack on the city of Chekhov set ​a warehouse alight and killed five people in the Novoselki industrial zone. Drones damaged a Wildberries warehouse near Krasny Bor in north-western Russia , wounding one person. A fire broke out when ​a drone ⁠fell on a distribution centre ⁠in the Leningrad region ​near ​St Petersburg operated ‌by Lenta, one ‌of the country’s largest food retailers, the company ‌said, with one person injured. Ukraine ⁠accused Russia of committing a war ⁠crime after a ​video was released showing a drone chasing down a street vendor and exploding in the southern Ukrainian city of Kherson. Police said the man in his 50s survived but suffered shock and shrapnel ⁠injuries, having dived under the vehicle for shelter. “Today, many were shocked by yet another video of the drone ‘safari’ Russians are carrying out against civilians in Kherson,” said Volodymyr ​Zelenskyy, Ukraine’s president. “We must act and support life in ways that force Russia to think seriously about peace rather than expanding ‌the range of its drones.” Small and lethal: adapted drones carrying explosives ‘hunt’ civilians in Kherson Read more Ukraine’s police and its foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, said the attack happened on Tuesday. Sybiha said the attack formed part of a deliberate Russian campaign to intimidate civilians . “This barbaric Russian war crime in Kherson demands international condemnation and justice, but thousands of similar crimes never come to the public eye.” The minister said the “sadist” pilot of the Russian drone would have known the target was a civilian. View image in fullscreen A picture released by Ukrainian’s national police shows a man selling vegetables being chased by a drone moments before it detonated, leaving him wounded and traumatised. Photograph: National Police of Ukraine/AFP/Getty Images Two children and an elderly woman were killed in Russian guided bomb strikes on Ukraine’s northern ​city of Sumy, said the regional governor, Oleh Hryhorov. Russia said seven people, including three children, were killed and 60 injured at its ​Black Sea holiday resort of ‌Gelendzhik by a Ukrainian drone. A Ukrainian official said the drone only fell on the beach because it was shot down by Russian air defences: “Ukraine uses its weapons exclusively against the Russian military-industrial complex and economic infrastructure facilities.” View image in fullscreen Mourners pay their respects to Vitalina Yarovenko who was killed helping survivors of a Russian attack on Kyiv. Photograph: Sergey Dolzhenko/EPA Hundreds of mourners dressed mostly in white walked through central Kyiv on Tuesday behind the open casket of a university student killed at the weekend by a Russian strike as she helped people wounded in an earlier attack . Vitalina Yarovenko’s mother had asked she be given the kind of funeral procession used in Ukraine to honour fallen soldiers. Several hundred people followed her casket. Traffic stopped to let the procession past while drivers stepped out of their cars and stood silently or knelt hand on heart. Russia has repeatedly targeted rescue workers by hitting residential buildings with two consecutive missiles: the first to draw crews to the scene and the second to wound or kill them. The tactic is called a “double tap” in military jargon. https://www.dw.com/en/norway-s-new-king-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JpFb King Haakon VIII swore to parliament to uphold the country's laws and constitution during his reign Image: Claudia Greco/REUTERS Advertisement New King Haakon VIII swore an oath of allegiance to Norway 's consititution in the parliament in Oslo on Tuesday, following him succeeding his father Harald V, who died last week . This follows a day after Harald's coffin was taken to the chapel of the royal palace, where it will remain for the public to pay their last respects until a funeral on September 9. Nowrway's Storting parliament was packed for the cermony Image: Claudia Greco/REUTERS What happened in the parliamentary ceremony? Haakon was driven the short distance from the royal palace to the Storting, or parliament in Oslo. House speaker Masud Gharahkhani read the official announcement of Harald's death and Haakon's succession before the new constitutional monarch took the oath. "I promise and swear that I will govern the Kingdom of Norway in according with its constitution and laws, so help me god, the almighty and omniscient," the 53-year-old said. Haakon's father Harald V died aged 89 last week, after a fairly protracted period of ailing health Image: Claudia Greco/REUTERS Queen Mette-Marit skips event amid complications following lung transplant Ahead of he ceremony, the palace said that Haakon's wife Queen Mette-Marit would not be attending. She had made her first public appearance since assuming the title on Monday in the coffin procession but is recovering after a lung transplant in June. In a statement, the palace quoted Are Holm, a pulmonologist at Oslo's University Hospital, as saying that complications following a transplant are not uncommon and that Mette-Marit had experienced them on several occasions, including Tuesday. "As a result, the Queen must remain under observation throughout the day. Unfortunately, the Queen will therefore be unable to attend the swearing-in ceremony at the Storting today," he said. People flocked to the royal palace to lay flowers and other signs of respect over the weekend Image: Hanna Johre/NTB/picture alliance What's the role of Norway's largely symbolic monarchy? Norway's royal family can trace its roots bak to the ninth century. When the country regained its independence from Sweden in 1905, three-quarters of voters supported the idea of reinstating a largely symbolic constitutional monarchy in a plebiscite. Most political power lies with the elected government and parliament, but Norway's royals retain a predominantly soft power role in diplomacy and promoting the country around the world. https://www.wral.com/news/ap/b8a0a-pope-.text: Pope Leo in Lourdes: What to know about one of Catholicism’s most famous pilgrimage sites PARIS (AP) — Pope Leo XIV is visiting the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes this weekend as part of his four-day apostolic journey to France, which is the first official papal state visit to the country in 18 years. Posted 9/24/2026, 4:23:10 AM Updated 9/27/2026, 7:03:11 AM Related Associated Press AP Religion AP World news People enter the Notre-Dame-du-Rosaire basilica in Lourdes, southwestern France, Tuesday Sept. 8, 2026 . (AP Photo/Fred Scheiber) By SAMUEL PETREQUIN — Associated Press PARIS (AP) — Pope Leo XIV is visiting the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes this weekend as part of his four-day apostolic journey to France, which is the first official papal state visit to the country in 18 years. The site near the Spanish border draws millions of pilgrims annually, including sick and disabled believers hoping for a cure from the famed spring water in the Lourdes grotto. Here is what to know about Lourdes, one of Catholicism’s most important pilgrimage sites. Other WRAL Top Stories The site began with Bernadette Soubirous Lourdes’ popularity is intrinsically linked to Bernadette Soubirous. A young girl who came from a modest background, she was uneducated, with no knowledge of religion, and suffered from asthma when she reported 18 visions of a lady dressed in white in the Grotto of Massabielle near Lourdes, between February and July 1858. The Catholic Church later accepted that the visions were of the Virgin Mary. Bernadette’s visions, and the subsequent discovery of allegedly healing spring waters, led the church to build a sanctuary there. In 1866, Bernadette left Lourdes to join the convent of the Sisters of Charity in Nevers, where she lived until her death at age 35. Pope Pius XI canonized her in 1933 as Saint Bernadette. Drinking the water of Lourdes: It's free Believers say that during the ninth apparition of the lady dressed in white, Bernadette heard her say: “Go and drink at the spring and wash yourself there.” Millions of pilgrims and visitors have since journeyed to Lourdes to drink and wash in this water, which has no therapeutic or specific properties. Lourdes water is free to access from the sanctuary’s taps and drinking fountains. Many pilgrims take some back home. Millions visit the grotto Lourdes became a major pilgrimage destination after the Catholic Church officially recognized Bernadette's visions as Apparitions in 1862. Since then, millions of pilgrims from around the world have flocked to the Grotto of Massabielle. As well as being a holy site, Lourdes attracts around 3 million pilgrims a year, including approximately 60,000 sick and disabled pilgrims. According to the town hall, it's the fourth most visited Catholic pilgrimage site in the world, after the Vatican, the Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe in Mexico City, and the Basilica of Our Lady of Aparecida in Brazil. Upon arrival Saturday night, Pope Leo prayed inside the Grotto of Apparitions and drank from the spring. A look at the sanctuary The Grotto of Massabielle is one of the 22 sites making up the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes. The sanctuary is home to numerous places of worship, including three basilicas: the Basilica of the Immaculate Conception, the oldest, the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary, and the underground Basilica of Saint Pius X. Pilgrims can also follow one of the two Stations of the Cross, featuring cast-iron or marble statues, before taking a dip in the sanctuary’s baths. There, they can immerse themselves in the 12 degrees Celsius (53.6 degrees Fahrenheit) water from the spring discovered in the Grotto of the Apparitions. 72 miraculous healings are recognized Among the millions traveling to Lourdes, many seek physical and spiritual healing, hoping for a miracle. The Catholic Church has officially recognized 72 healings as miraculous at Lourdes, out of more than 7,000 cases examined since 1858. Hotel rooms galore, but prices through the roof Less than 15,000 people actually live in Lourdes. But with nearly 10,000 hotel rooms and around 21,200 beds, it has the second-largest hotel capacity in France, after Paris. Finding an affordable roof over your head during Leo's visit, however, is a tall order. The pope's visit will draw hundreds of thousands of visitors, sending accommodation prices skyrocketing. Some hoteliers are charging extremely high rates, sometimes reaching more than 2,000 euros ($2,300) per night. Pilgrims from Eastern and Central Europe are fans Even though most pilgrims traveling to Lourdes each year come from France — 42%, according to the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes — many visitors from Eastern Europe are expected to come and greet Leo. Following the end of the Cold War, Catholics from Central and Eastern Europe gained the freedom to go west, sharply increasing the number of pilgrims from former Communist countries visiting Lourdes. This trend has continued to the present day. Poland ranks sixth among the more than 160 nations sending pilgrims to Lourdes each year. The controversial mosaics are covered Leo won't get a glimpse of the mosaics by an ex-Jesuit artist accused of abusing women adorning the façade of the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary. They will all be covered during Leo's visit. The artwork was made by Rev. Marko Ivan Rupnik, a Slovenian artist whose mosaic designs decorate Vatican chapels and churches and basilicas around the world. The Vatican confirmed this summer that a church trial against Rupnik is ongoing. Lourdes Bishop Jean-Marc Micas announced the move last month, after a decision two years ago that the mosaics would no longer be lit during evening prayer. In March 2025, the mosaics on the basilica's entrance doors had already been covered. The Rupnik scandal exploded publicly in late 2022, when Italian blogs first reported claims by women and nuns of sexual, spiritual and psychological abuse by Rupnik dating back to the 1990s that had been consistently dismissed by the Catholic hierarchy. Leo will meet bishops and assault survivors Leo will meet seven survivors of sexual abuse who were assaulted as children or adults, according to the Bishops’ Conference of France. A 2021 report estimated that 330,000 children had been sexually abused over 70 years by church personnel in France. The Lourdes sanctuary said the pope will land at the Tarbes airport on Saturday and begin his pilgrimage with a prayer at the Grotto of the Apparitions. On Sunday morning, Leo will meet with the bishops at the French Bishops’ Conference, then celebrate Mass on the Prairie, followed by the Angelus prayer. In the afternoon, he will meet the staff and sick people of the Accueil Notre-Dame. He closes the visit with one of Lourdes’ signature rites: the Rosary and torchlight procession through the sanctuary. Copyright 2026 by The Associated Press. All rights reserved.
